title: SQL Foundations
subtitle: Learn to read tables, write SELECT queries, filter rows, sort results, and handle real-world beginner data.
intendedFor: web developers who need SQL basics
learningGoals: Explain what SQL does in plain language.
Identify tables, rows, columns, records, fields, and simple keys.
Write basic SELECT queries against one table.
Choose specific columns instead of always using SELECT *.
Filter rows with WHERE.
Compare text and numeric values.
Combine conditions with AND, OR, and NOT.
Sort results with ORDER BY.
Limit output with LIMIT.
Search text using LIKE and wildcards.
Filter lists and ranges using IN, NOT IN, and BETWEEN.
Find missing values using IS NULL and IS NOT NULL.
Read query results and explain them in plain English.

modules.title: Getting Started with SQL and Databases
modules.purpose: Build the learner's mental model before syntax: what SQL is, how databases organize information, and how questions become queries.
learningObjectives: Explain what SQL is used for in real applications.
Identify tables, rows, columns, records, and fields.
Read simple table data and describe what it means.
Use the browser SQL workspace to run a beginner query.

topics.title: What SQL Is
topics.summary: Meet SQL as a language for asking useful questions of organized data.
learningGoals: Explain what SQL is used for without relying on query syntax.
Describe a database as organized stored data that software can work with.
Connect a real-world question to the idea of asking a database for a result.

topics.title: Understanding Tables
topics.summary: Read a table by separating its columns, rows, records, and fields.
learningGoals: Distinguish a table, row, and column in a simple database.
Relate record to row and field to column without treating the terms as different structures.
Read table and column names from a small schema before writing queries.

topics.title: Database Thinking
topics.summary: Think about the question, the structure of the data, and how one record can be identified reliably.
learningGoals: Turn a plain-language question into the data fields needed to answer it.
Explain why consistent structure makes stored data easier to inspect and query.
Explain why a stable identifier is safer than a display name for identifying one record.

topics.title: First SQL Environment
topics.summary: Use the SQL editor, Run button, Results view, and Tables view without learning extra query syntax too early.
learningGoals: Identify the SQL editor, Run action, and results area in the course workspace.
Run one small SQL statement and inspect the returned result.
Use the Tables view to confirm what data is available before querying it.

topics.title: Module 0 Student Roster Project
topics.summary: Build a simple student roster snapshot one safe SELECT step at a time until the final table is ready to share.
learningGoals: Keep a small SQL project growing from one working query to the next.
Read a student table by selecting the columns needed for a clear roster view.

modules.moduleProject: Create a simple data map for a tiny school or store database showing tables, columns, and example rows.

modules.title: Your First Queries with SELECT
modules.purpose: Teach learners to retrieve data confidently with SELECT and FROM before filtering or joining tables.
learningObjectives: Write SELECT queries that retrieve data from one table.
Choose specific columns instead of always selecting every column.
Use FROM to identify the table being queried.
Read a query result table and explain what was returned.

topics.title: What SELECT Does
topics.summary: Understand what select does so you can explain the idea in beginner-friendly language.
learningGoals: Explain the different jobs of SELECT and FROM in a single-table query.
Write a complete beginner retrieval query with requested columns and a source table.
Predict which result columns a SELECT list will produce.

topics.title: Selecting Specific Columns
topics.summary: Practice selecting specific columns so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Explain when SELECT * is useful for exploration and when explicit columns are better.
Select only the columns required for a task.
Control the left-to-right result order through the SELECT list.

topics.title: Query Multiple Columns
topics.summary: Practice query multiple columns so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Separate multiple selected columns correctly with commas.
Control result-column order by arranging the SELECT list intentionally.
Format a multi-column query so it is easy to review without changing its behavior.

topics.title: Common Beginner Syntax Mistakes
topics.summary: Practice common beginner syntax mistakes so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Predict the columns a simple SELECT query should return before running it.
Recognize common beginner mistakes involving commas, clause order, and schema names.
Repair a broken single-table query using a small syntax checklist.

topics.title: Module 1 Product Starter Sheet Project
topics.summary: Build a clean product starter sheet by growing one SELECT query into a simple reference report.
learningGoals: Carry a product query forward from one finished step to the next.
Select only the product columns that make a report easier to read.

modules.moduleProject: Build a starter query sheet with beginner SELECT queries against a products table.

modules.title: Filtering Data with WHERE
modules.purpose: Introduce decision-making in queries by teaching learners to keep only the rows they actually need.
learningObjectives: Use WHERE to return only rows that match a condition.
Compare text and numbers with beginner SQL operators.
Combine conditions with AND, OR, and NOT.
Debug common filtering mistakes in simple SQL queries.

topics.title: Why Filtering Matters
topics.summary: Understand why filtering matters so you can explain the idea in beginner-friendly language.
learningGoals: Explain how WHERE changes a query result without modifying stored data.
Place WHERE after FROM in a simple single-table query.
Translate a plain-language filtering request into one row condition.

topics.title: Equals Comparison
topics.summary: Practice equals comparison so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Use = to keep rows with one exact known value.
Use <> to exclude one exact known value.
Quote text comparison values correctly while leaving column names unquoted.

topics.title: Greater-Than Comparison
topics.summary: Practice greater-than comparison so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Distinguish strict comparisons > and < from inclusive comparisons >= and <=.
Translate boundary wording such as at least and at most into the correct operator.
Check whether the boundary row should be included before choosing an operator.

topics.title: Filtering Numbers and Text
topics.summary: Practice filtering numbers and text so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Write numeric comparison values without quotes and text values with single quotes.
Choose an operator that matches the wording of the filtering request.
Separate literal-format decisions from boundary-operator decisions.

topics.title: AND Conditions
topics.summary: Practice and conditions so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Use AND when all listed filtering rules must be satisfied.
Use OR when any listed alternative may satisfy the request.
Translate plain-language simultaneous requirements and alternatives into logical conditions.

topics.title: Combining Conditions Safely
topics.summary: Practice combining conditions safely so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Use parentheses to make mixed AND/OR logic explicit.
Explain how grouping changes which rows satisfy a mixed condition.
Use NOT deliberately and prefer a simpler equivalent comparison when it is clearer.

topics.title: Avoiding Filtering Mistakes
topics.summary: Practice avoiding filtering mistakes so you can use it in a simple SQL query or workflow.
learningGoals: Distinguish a syntactically valid filter from a logically correct filter.
Diagnose common filtering mistakes involving operators, quoting, AND/OR, and clause order.
Repair one filtering problem at a time and verify the result against the requirement.

topics.title: Module 2 Inventory Watchlist Project
topics.summary: Build an inventory watchlist by adding one practical filter at a time to the same working query.
learningGoals: Refine one inventory query through multiple filtering steps.
Use comparisons and logical conditions to isolate the products that need attention.

modules.moduleProject: Create a data-detective worksheet with filtering prompts and SQL answers.

modules.title: Sorting and Limiting Results
modules.purpose: Help beginners control output so answers are easier to read, rank, and compare.
learningObjectives: Sort query results with ORDER BY.
Use ASC and DESC to control sort direction.
Use LIMIT to show a smaller result set.
Combine filtering, sorting, and limiting in one query.

topics.title: Sorting a Result with ORDER BY
topics.summary: Use ORDER BY after row selection to change result order without changing which rows belong in the result.
learningGoals: Explain that ORDER BY changes result sequence rather than row membership.
Place ORDER BY after FROM and WHERE in a simple query.
Sort a single result column in a requested presentation order.

topics.title: Choosing ASC or DESC
topics.summary: Choose ascending or descending direction from the business meaning of first, last, smallest, largest, earliest, or latest.
learningGoals: Explain the direction produced by ASC for text, numbers, and dates.
Explain the direction produced by DESC for text, numbers, and dates.
Translate ranking language such as highest first or earliest first into the correct direction.

topics.title: Primary Sorts and Tie-Breakers
topics.summary: Use a second ORDER BY column to create a predictable order inside rows that share the same primary value.
learningGoals: Identify the primary sort in a multi-column ORDER BY clause.
Explain when and why a secondary sort acts as a tie-breaker.
Write a two-column ORDER BY clause in the requested priority order.

topics.title: Building Ranked Top-N Results with LIMIT
topics.summary: Sort first when a request asks for top, bottom, cheapest, newest, or similar ranked rows, then limit that ordered result.
learningGoals: Explain why LIMIT alone does not define a top or bottom ranking.
Place LIMIT after ORDER BY in a ranked query.
Combine filtering, ranking, and a row limit to answer a top-N or bottom-N request.

topics.title: Module 3 Sales Leaderboard Project
topics.summary: Turn a rough product query into a ranked leaderboard by layering sorting and limiting steps one by one.
learningGoals: Grow a ranking query from a plain result set into a focused leaderboard.
Use ORDER BY and LIMIT to make a product report easy to scan.

modules.moduleProject: Build a ranked product report using sorting and limiting.

modules.title: Working with Text, Lists, Ranges, and NULL
modules.purpose: Expand filtering to real-world cases like partial text, multiple choices, ranges, and missing values.
learningObjectives: Search partial text with LIKE and wildcards.
Filter multiple values with IN and NOT IN.
Filter ranges with BETWEEN.
Find missing and present values with IS NULL and IS NOT NULL.

topics.title: Matching Text with LIKE and %
topics.summary: Use LIKE with the percent wildcard to match text prefixes, suffixes, and contained fragments.
learningGoals: Explain how LIKE differs from an exact equality comparison.
Interpret percent-wildcard patterns for starts-with, ends-with, and contains searches.
Write a LIKE filter that matches a required text prefix.

topics.title: Matching Exact Character Positions with _
topics.summary: Use the underscore wildcard when a pattern needs exactly one character in a specific position.
learningGoals: Explain that underscore matches exactly one character in a LIKE pattern.
Distinguish fixed-length underscore matching from variable-length percent matching.
Write a pattern that constrains one unknown character at a specific position.

topics.title: Filtering Exact Sets with IN and NOT IN
topics.summary: Use IN for several allowed exact values and NOT IN for several excluded exact values.
learningGoals: Explain that IN matches any one exact value from a list.
Contrast IN with repeated OR comparisons and NOT IN with exclusions.
Write an IN filter for a small set of allowed text values.

topics.title: Filtering Inclusive Ranges with BETWEEN
topics.summary: Use BETWEEN for an inclusive lower-and-upper range, and combine it with other conditions when needed.
learningGoals: Explain that BETWEEN includes both lower and upper endpoints.
Translate BETWEEN into equivalent greater-than-or-equal and less-than-or-equal logic.
Write an inclusive date-range filter with correctly ordered boundaries.

topics.title: Understanding NULL and Missing Values
topics.summary: Treat NULL as missing or unknown data and use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL instead of normal equality.
learningGoals: Explain what NULL represents and distinguish it from empty text or zero.
Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL for missing-value checks.
Recognize why = NULL is not the correct way to filter missing data.

topics.title: Combining Text and Missing-Value Rules
topics.summary: Combine LIKE, NULL checks, AND, OR, and parentheses to express practical cleanup rules clearly.
learningGoals: Choose LIKE versus NULL operators based on whether the rule concerns text shape or value presence.
Combine text and missing-value conditions with AND or OR.
Use parentheses to make mixed AND/OR cleanup logic explicit.

topics.title: Module 4 Customer Cleanup Project
topics.summary: Build a cumulative customer-cleanup report with NULL, exact-value, text-pattern, and test-record filters.
learningGoals: Carry a correct SQL query forward across cumulative project milestones.
Combine NULL checks, exact-value filters, LIKE patterns, and AND conditions.
Produce a final cleanup result that satisfies a concrete stakeholder handoff.

modules.moduleProject: Create a search-and-cleanup worksheet for a customer table with missing or inconsistent information.

modules.title: Capstone: Customer Follow-Up Report
modules.purpose: Pull the course skills together in one final reporting task that feels like a beginner analyst handoff.
learningObjectives: Combine selection, filtering, ordering, and limiting in one practical query flow.
Revise a working query without losing earlier progress.
Build a clean report that highlights real customer follow-up needs.

topics.title: Module 5 Customer Follow-Up Capstone
topics.summary: Build a cumulative stakeholder report using status lists, NULL checks, exact-value filters, ranges, LIKE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT.
learningGoals: Carry a correct SQL query forward through four cumulative stakeholder requirements.
Combine IN, IS NOT NULL, exact comparisons, BETWEEN, and LIKE in one readable WHERE clause.
Apply ORDER BY before LIMIT so the final five-row handoff is deterministic.
Preserve approved requirements while extending a query instead of rewriting it from scratch.

projectBrief.scenario: A community outreach coordinator needs a concise customer follow-up list built from the cleanup table. The report must keep only useful, contactable records and rank the most recent signups first.
projectBrief.role: Junior SQL analyst preparing a customer follow-up handoff
projectBrief.workspace: Browser SQL editor, customers table schema, and deterministic results table
projectBrief.deliverable: One four-step cumulative customer follow-up query that combines the core SQL Foundations skills without losing earlier requirements.
requirements: Keep one valid SELECT statement in every step.
Use the previous complete solution as the next starter query.
Preserve every earlier requirement unless the current step explicitly replaces it.
Use only SQL concepts taught in SQL Foundations.
Finish with deterministic ordering and a practical row limit.

stepLadder.title: Build the Follow-Up Candidate List
stepLadder.requirement: Return the requested customer columns and keep only records whose status is active or draft using IN.

stepLadder.title: Keep Contactable Customers
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve the candidate list and require a non-missing email address with IS NOT NULL.

stepLadder.title: Apply the Date and Text Rules
stepLadder.requirement: Keep all prior filters, add the authored signup-date range with BETWEEN, and exclude test-style names with a LIKE-based condition.

stepLadder.title: Rank and Limit the Final Handoff
stepLadder.requirement: Preserve every filter, sort the newest signups first with a stable secondary sort, and limit the report to the requested number of rows.

modules.moduleProject: Create a final customer follow-up report that surfaces the most important real records for a teammate to review.
